The expression equals $\dfrac{\omega^5-1}{\omega-1}$ for $\omega\neq1$. Since $\omega^5=2$, we have $\omega\ne1$, and the expression simplifies to $\dfrac{1}{\omega-1}$.

The five roots of $P(x)=x^5-2$ are distinct, so we need $\sum \dfrac{1}{\omega-1}$ over all of them.

For a polynomial with roots $\omega_i$, $\dfrac{P'(x)}{P(x)}=\sum \dfrac{1}{x-\omega_i}$. At $x=1$:

$$\sum \frac{1}{1-\omega_i}=\frac{P'(1)}{P(1)}=\frac{5}{1-2}=-5.$$

Therefore $\sum \dfrac{1}{\omega_i-1}=5$.

The five values $\dfrac{1}{\omega-1}$ are distinct because the roots are distinct, so their sum is the sum of all possible values.

ANSWER: 5
